problem:
Evaluate the following integral of a vector-valued function. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{1}^{8}⟨5t-2,\,\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{t}^{2}}}⟩\,\text{d}t=⟨$
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}} $⟩$
worked_solution:
To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{8}⟨5t-2,\,\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{t}^{2}}}⟩\,\text{d}t & =⟨{\int }_{1}^{8}(5t-2)\,\text{d}t,\,{\int }_{1}^{8}\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{t}^{2}}}\,\text{d}t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

For the first component, we integrate directly:

$$
\int (5t-2)\,\text{d}t=\frac{5}{2}{t}^{2}-2t.
$$

For the second component, we write 

$$
\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{t}^{2}}}=\frac{1}{3}{t}^{-2/3}
$$

and integrate:

$$
\int \frac{1}{3}{t}^{-2/3}\,\text{d}t=\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{{t}^{1/3}}{1/3}={t}^{1/3}.
$$

Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{8}⟨5t-2,\,\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{t}^{2}}}⟩\,\text{d}t & =⟨(\frac{5}{2}{t}^{2}-2t){|}_{1}^{8},\,({t}^{1/3}){|}_{1}^{8}⟩ \\  & =⟨(\frac{5}{2}\cdot 64-16)-(\frac{5}{2}\cdot 1-2),\,2-1⟩ \\  & =⟨144-\frac{1}{2},\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{287}{2},\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{287}{2},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
